procedural_matters: GBR was represented by Marcus King.
ITA was represented by Lorenzo Sirena.
Race Committee was represented by Bence Kárpáti (World Sailing Course Representative).
Maddie Jinks (GBR crew) and Gianluka Piccino (ITA coach) attended the hearing as an observer.
Jonathan McGovern (GBR coach) was a witness for GBR and presented tracking evidence.
Patric Loydell (Member of the International Jury) presented evidence.
Hearing No. 2 was heard together with hearing No. 4 in accordance with RRS 63.2(b) since both hearings arose from the same incident.
facts: Before the competitors had rounded the leeward gate during race 1, the Race Committee displayed Flag C and green with sound signals, and proceeded to move the mark into its new location.
When ITA rounded the leeward gate, they were in 1st position and GBR in 2nd.
When GBR and ITA were 50-80m from the windward mark, it was still motoring into its new location.
The mark continued motoring for approximately 30m, before reaching its new location.
GBR and ITA proceeded to sail towards and round a pink robotic mark.
The windward mark of the Multihull course is described in the SI as a Yellow robotic mark.
GBR and ITA did not round their Yellow windward mark.
GBR finished in 6th position and ITA in 1st position.
GBR and ITA were scored NSC.
conclusions: By having the windward mark motoring into location when the leaders were 50-80m away from the mark, the Race Committee made an improper action however GBR and ITA’s place in race 1 was made significantly worse through their own fault by not rounding the windward mark of their course. Therefore the requirements in 61.4(b)(1) are not met.
By scoring ITA and GBR NSC in Race 1, the Race Committee did not make an improper action.
